key_insight: LLMs labeled incidental findings in lung cancer screening CT reports with moderate to almost perfect agreement, but no model–prompt combination performed best across all findings.
clinical_relevance: This report-labeling study—not cancer drug discovery research—suggests potential to support incidental-finding data extraction for lung screening research.
method: Retrospective analysis of 300 CT reports from one Dutch academic hospital.
Compared four LLMs and keyword search for labeling nine specific incidental findings against a radiologist reference.
Tested four prompting strategies per LLM, with and without chain-of-thought.
evidence_signal: GPT-5 achieved Cohen’s κ of 0.71–0.97 for seven findings; the best reported agreement for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass was moderate (κ=0.48 and 0.42, respectively).
watch_item: Single-center results and finding-dependent performance warrant external validation before clinical workflow use.
paper_title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
